default._resident_note_1033: **#1033 device-mounted volume sets, after the RAM audit: 440,984 → 458,600 B (+17,616).** The explicit set residents are caller-placed `set_shards` 4,844 B, `set_sources` 88 B, and the 14,212 B `set_extent_tables` slot: 11 × 1,292 B tables with a set-specific 64-run cap. That slot is a size/alignment-pinned union with the pre-existing 2,060 B standalone-map table because boot selects exactly one map kind and never switches it; subtracting the standalone table already present at the base makes the net explicit-static increase 17,084 B. Retaining every shard handle in `Storage::open_set` accounts for 532 B more (`__embassy_main::POOL` 32,592 → 32,968, +376; `SHARED_STORE` 6,368 → 6,524, +156). Standalone maps keep their proven 128-run cap. A set shard over 64 runs is refused with its true count and fixed by re-copying; 64 remains above the reference card's worst measured 46-run map. The parsed 832 B manifest is now mount-time-only in an out-of-line synchronous frame, while `MountedSet` retains a one-byte core index and remains 20 B. The guarded poll frame stays 9,728 B. Linked residents leave 53,400 B below the 500 KiB M33 carve—17,592 B above the last measured 35,808 B deep ride-path peak—so the shard-junction route and finish/save path remain the on-glass acceptance before merge. CI run 30646341768 links flash at **1,257,640 B** on both profiles: 1,236,752 → 1,257,640 (+20,888), so `measured_flash` below is authoritative.
default._resident_note: **Fix round (review of #1040): resident unmoved at 440,984 B, flash +7,328 B.** Nine findings' worth of correctness work and not one resident byte: `sd::Storage::open_upload` gained an owner tag (`Option<RawFile>` → `Option<(RawFile, UploadOwner)>`, so a BLE teardown can no longer close the handle the cable is streaming a set into), the cross-transport one-transfer gate became `obc_app::TransferGate` (an `AtomicU8` holding *which wire* claimed it, where an `AtomicBool` let a phone dropping off the radio release a gate the cable held), and the boot sweep swapped two bounded `heapless::Vec`s of directory entries for two 125-byte id bitmaps. All three land inside existing padding or replace something the same size — `.bss` 435,840 B and `.data` 5,144 B are byte-identical to the pre-fix tree, `.uninit` is unmoved at 1,024 B, the poll frame is unmoved at 9,728 B, and all 23 `compile_time_allocations` entries match without a single change. Flash is the only mover, and it is now a **measurement rather than a projection**: the `embedded` job (run 30610810321) links **1,236,752 B** on both the `default` and `ble` legs — 1,218,184 → 1,236,752, +18,568 B for the whole PR, of which the fix round is +7,328 as measured on the pinned host (1,259,944 → 1,267,272 at `default`; local hosts link a different absolute figure, which is why flash is not gated for board profiles and why the number below is CI's). The fix round's share is the enforcement itself — the `NotFound` arm in `delete_set`, the torn/short magic verdicts, the id-space and free-space announce refusals, the abort path into the set session, the allocator's directory walk, and the sweep's two-pass bitmap scan. Previously: 440,960 → 440,984 B (+24) for the volume-set receive path (#1039, epic #1016 P3b). A set is `1..=32` shards plus a manifest, so unlike every other object type its correctness lives *between* transfers and the device must remember what it has: `ObjectStore` gains `set_upload: Option<obc_app::SetUpload>`, which is a set id `u16`, a shard count `u8` and a 32-bit committed bitmap — 8 B plus the `Option` discriminant at align 4. Itemized by symbol diff against the identical tree at the merge base, and the four movers account for the 24 B exactly: `link::STORE` 13,528 → 13,540 (+12 — that field, in the one resident `ObjectStore`); `usb::data_plane::TRANSFER_ARM` and `ble::state::TRANSFER_ARM` 32 → 36 each (+8 total — the `Signal<Armed>` handoff, because `Armed` gained `SetShard(TransferControl, Receiver, SetPart)`, its widest variant); and the merged small-statics group `.L_MergedGlobals` 108 → 112 (+4, padding after that shift — the seven renumbered `.L_MergedGlobals.*` groups sum to 776 B on both sides). Nothing else moved: no new `.bss` buffer, and the manifest work deliberately owns none — `Storage::validate_committed_manifest` puts its 1,864 B `MAX_MANIFEST_LEN` buffer on an `#[inline(never)]` frame that is gone before the commit write, and `sweep_aborted_sets` is a boot-time frame, so the ~36 KB stack rule is respected rather than paid for in residency. `compile_time_allocations` moves in the two entries that are the same 12 B seen twice: `ble_object_store` 13,528 → 13,540 and its `ble_total` 37,570 → 37,582. Poll frame unmoved at 9,728 B; `.uninit` unmoved at 1,024 B; the `default` and `ble` legs link the identical 440,984 B on the pinned host. **Flash is a projection, not a measurement**: it is not gated for board profiles and CI is the authority, so `measured_flash` below is the previous CI figure plus this change's locally-measured delta (+13,208 B: 1,246,736 → 1,259,944 on the pinned host at the `default` profile) and must be re-pinned from this PR's `embedded` run. Previously: 439,040 → 440,960 B (+1,920) for the volume-set FAT handle budget (#1026, epic #1016 P3b). `OBCA_Spec.md` §5 makes one logical map 1..32 physical files, and the epic's device-cost review requires a mounted set to hold **every** shard's handle open for the mount lifetime — re-opening per query would put a FAT directory walk in the render loop. `sd::SD_MAX_FILES` therefore goes 6 → 16: the 8 handles a DACH-shaped set needs (core + coarse + ~6 geometry) plus the unchanged 5-handle mid-ride peak documented above `SdSpi`, plus margin. The ceiling that leaves is stated rather than implied: `sd::SD_SET_MAX_SHARDS` = `SD_MAX_FILES − SD_RIDE_PEAK_FILES` = **11 shards**, against `OBCA_Spec.md` §5.2's cap of 32 — a larger set is refused at mount with `obc_reader::MountError::Handles(11)`, naming this device's cap, instead of failing an open mid-ride. **The whole increase is that one constant, and it costs 3× what the array does.** The fork's `FileInfo` (`filesystem/files.rs`) is `RawFile` 4 · `RawVolume` 4 · `current_cluster` 8 · `current_offset` 4 · `Mode` 1 · `DirEntry` 40 · `dirty` 1 = 64 B at align 4 on thumbv8m, held in `VolumeManager`'s `heapless::Vec<FileInfo, SD_MAX_FILES>`; ten more slots is 640 B per resident `VolumeManager`, and the image links **three**. Itemized by symbol diff against the identical tree with the constant back at 6: `__embassy_main::POOL` 31,312 → 32,592 (+1,280 — *two* copies of `Storage` inside main's async frame, because an async frame allocates every local at entry, the same #270 trap that put `MAP_EXTENTS` in its own `.bss` slot rather than inside `Storage`) and `SHARED_STORE` 5,728 → 6,368 (+640 — the copy that actually lives for the session). Nothing else moved: the same tree with `SD_MAX_FILES = 6` links exactly 439,040 B, so the rest of #1026 — the `MapSummary` growth for sets, `set_identity`, `delete_set`, the `MapChoice::set` field — costs **zero** resident bytes. Re-measured after the review fix round (the `SetShards` split, the ladder/version/handle mount checks, the shard-reader nav/POI guards, the pure entry classifier and delete plan): the same tree with `SD_MAX_FILES = 6` still links exactly 439,040 B, so none of those cost resident bytes either, and the fix round's own headline — `obc_reader::MountedSet` going from 14,924 B by value to 20 B, with the 14,084 B shard table moved into a caller-placed `SetShards` — does not appear here at all, because nothing on the device mounts a set yet: it is a *stack/frame* cost this PR makes impossible to incur later, not a `.bss` one, and the compile-time allocation table is unchanged in all 23 entries. Poll frame unmoved at 9,728 B. Figures are **CI's** (the `embedded` job is the gate); this is a case where the pinned local host links the *identical* 440,960 B, and CI's `default` and `ble` legs agree byte for byte (run 30589233369: 440,960 B linked resident, flash 1,218,184 B on both legs), which is where `measured_flash` below comes from. Previously: 438,912 → 439,040 B (+128) for the OBCM v11 chunk-offset table (#1009), stacked on the #889 staging buffer below — the two are independent. The whole increase is one field, counted twice: `obc_reader::Lod` gained `chunk_bytes_total: usize` (the LOD's total chunk bytes, `offsets[Chunk Count]`, kept resident so a per-chunk fetch bounds its offset pair without a second read), and the reader holds `Vec<Lod, 16>` — so 4 B × 16 slots = 64 B per `MapTables`, of which the image has two: the static `MAP_TABLES` (4,060 → 4,124, see `compile_time_allocations`) and the copy inside the embassy task pool future. Measured on the merge of #1014 into this branch: 439,040 B, i.e. exactly the +128 it linked against the pre-#1014 base, so the offset table costs the same either side of that merge. Both figures are confirmed against this merge's own `embedded` run (30522203604): 439,040 B linked resident and flash 1,209,608 B, identical on the `default` and `ble` legs, and `measured_flash` below is taken from that log (local hosts link a different flash figure; flash is not gated for board profiles). The v11 offset table itself is *file* bytes, not resident ones, and buys back ~2.3× on every map. Poll frame unmoved at 9,728 B. Previously: 422,504 → 438,912 B (+16,408) for the map-upload staging buffer (#889). Figures are **CI's** (the `embedded` job is the gate); this increase is the rare case where the pinned local host links the **identical** 438,912 B and CI's `default` and `ble` legs agree byte for byte (run 30520773708). The increase is one named allocation plus its future: `usb_named` 2,652 → 19,036 (+16,384) is `usb::STAGE_LEN`, a 16 KiB `.bss` buffer the USB data plane fills from the bulk endpoint and drains to the card a batch at a time. It exists because the embedded-sdmmc fork can only issue an ACMD23+CMD25 multi-block write for what one `VolumeManager::write` hands it, and the plane previously handed it one 512 B packet at a time — 2,458 µs/block against 478 at 64-block batches (`sd_bench` `wr-*`, on glass). The remaining +24 B is the USB data-plane task's `TaskStorage`: `run_upload`'s future gained one `link::stage::Stage` local (a `&mut [u8]` fat pointer plus two `usize` counters), and embassy sizes task storage from the future. 16 KiB and not 32: it takes ~94% of the batching win, and the second 16 KiB would halve the margin between the ~72 KiB residual stack and the 35,808 B measured deep-ride peak — this is the crate where async frames overflow silently. Poll frame unmoved at 9,728 B. Previously: 422,208 → 422,504 B (+296) for the `Next: <category>` stat fields' per-category cache (#951, epic #946, U5). Figures are **CI's** (the `embedded` job is the gate and runs floating stable); the pinned local host links 8 B less resident (422,496 measured here) and a different flash figure, neither of which is gated — Both resident figures were **confirmed against the `embedded` job** (run 30371199831: 422,504 B linked resident, `app` 136,504 B, identical on the `default` and `ble` legs), and `measured_flash` below is taken from the same log. The whole increase is one named allocation: `app` 136,208 → 136,504 (+296), i.e. `size_of::<App>()`. It is the new `UiRuntime::next_ahead` (`NextAhead`): six cache lines of `Option<NextPoi { u32, String<24> }>` + an `Option<u32>` take anchor, plus the scheduler's request/turn/route fields. Held once in `App` for the same #425 reason as `poi_scratch` and `corridor_scratch` — a `Screen` variant is a slot in a `.bss` union, so inline it would multiply across all 10 stack slots. It buys the stat tiles their answer *without* a second 16-slot corridor buffer: the snapshot is distilled to one `(dist_along_m, name)` per category and the shared `CorridorScratch` is reused as-is. Poll frame unmoved at 9,728 B. Previously: 422,080 → 422,208 B (+128) and flash 1,190,108 → 1,189,884 for the OBCR v3 waypoint record (#947). Figures are **CI's** (the `embedded` job is the gate and runs floating stable); the pinned local host links 8 B less resident and a different flash figure, neither of which is gated. The whole increase is one named allocation: `app` 136,080 → 136,208 — the resident `Waypoints` table's 32 × `WptEntry` at +4 B each, the entry having gained `category: Option<PoiCategory>` (1 B, niche-packed) and `lateral_offset_m: i16`, which fit in the record's existing tail padding. Nothing else moved, and flash *fell* 224 B (the reader lost its two-version branches). Poll frame unmoved at 9,728 B. Previously: 421,224 → 422,080 B (+856) and flash 1,185,668 → 1,190,108 for the route-corridor POI snapshot (#948, epic #946). Figures are **CI's** (the `embedded` job is the gate and runs floating stable); the pinned local host links 8 B less resident, the usual layout difference, and a different flash figure — neither is gated. The whole increase is **one named allocation**: `app` 135,224 → 136,080 B (+856), i.e. `size_of::<App>()`. Nothing else moved — the delta and the `app` delta are the same 856 bytes. It is the new `UiRuntime::corridor_scratch` (`CorridorScratch`): a 16-slot `heapless::Vec<CorridorPoi>` (16 × 52 B = 832) plus its `want`/`taken_for` snapshot keys. Held once in `App` **by design**, exactly like `poi_scratch` before it — inline in the `Screen` union it would multiply across all 10 stack slots (~8.6 KB) instead of costing the buffer once (issue #425). Poll frame unmoved at 9,728 B.

It is the new `UiRuntime::corridor_scratch` (`CorridorScratch`): a 16-slot `heapless::Vec<CorridorPoi>` (16 × 52 B = 832) plus its `want`/`taken_for` snapshot keys. Held once in `App` **by design**, exactly like `poi_scratch` before it — inline in the `Screen` union it would multiply across all 10 stack slots (~8.6 KB) instead of costing the buffer once (issue #425). Poll frame unmoved at 9,728 B.
